i-love-you-hand.context: A raised hand with the thumb, index finger and little finger extended and the middle two fingers folded down. Used for the I love you hand sign in sign language apps, messages of affection and deaf culture content.

shushing.context: A face with an index finger held upright against the lips. Used for quiet zones, silent mode, secrets and please be quiet notices in libraries and chat reactions.

holding-hands.context: Two people standing side by side holding hands. Used for friendship, couples, companionship, togetherness and support services such as buddy schemes and dating.

finger-snap.context: A hand with the thumb and middle finger pressed together and short sparks at the fingertips. Used for instant actions, quick results, magic and rhythm or music apps.

offering-hand.context: An open hand held out palm up with a small ball resting on it. Used for offering, giving, sharing, donations, handing something over and customer service.

timeout-gesture.context: Two flat hands forming a T shape, one held upright with the other resting across its fingertips. Used to call a time out, request a break or pause in sports, meetings and games.

arms-crossed.context: A person with both forearms folded across the chest. Used for waiting, impatience, disapproval, defensive body language and not impressed reactions.

hands-on-hips.context: A standing figure with the elbows out and both hands resting on the hips. Used for confidence, impatience, power poses and body language guides.

shrug.context: A figure with raised shoulders and both forearms turned out with the palms up. Used for I don't know, no idea, whatever and uncertain answers in chat and help content.

salute.context: A standing figure raising a flat hand to the brow in a salute. Used for respect, military and veterans content, honour and acknowledging an order.

bowing-person.context: A standing figure bent forward at the waist in a polite bow. Used for respect, thanks, apologies, greetings and etiquette guides.

curtsy.context: A figure in a flared skirt holding its edges out to the sides in a curtsy. Used for polite greetings, ballet and dance, royal etiquette and taking a bow after a performance.

fist-palm-salute.context: A closed fist pressed into an open flat palm, a traditional greeting of respect. Used for martial arts classes, Lunar New Year greetings, congratulations and thanks.

nodding-yes.context: A smiling face with curved motion arcs above and below, showing a nod. Used for yes, agreement, approval and consent in chat, surveys and accessibility controls.

shaking-head-no.context: A face with curved motion arcs on both sides, showing the head shaking from side to side. Used for no, disagreement, refusal and declining in chat and feedback.

wagging-finger.context: A raised index finger with motion arcs on both sides, wagging back and forth. Used for no no, warnings, telling off, not allowed notices and scolding reactions.

hand-over-mouth.context: A wide-eyed face with one hand covering the mouth. Used for shock, surprise, oops moments, embarrassment and speechless reactions in chat.

counting-on-fingers.context: A raised hand with three fingers up and a dot above each fingertip. Used for counting, numbers, tallies, early maths and step by step lessons.

arms-x-sign.context: A person with both forearms crossed in front of the chest to form a large X. Used for no, stop, wrong answers, not allowed and cancel gestures.

open-arms.context: A standing figure with both arms spread wide and slightly raised. Used for welcome messages, hugs, openness, freedom and community or inclusion themes.

surrender-pose.context: A standing figure with both arms raised straight up. Used for hands up, surrender, giving up, arrests and I give in reactions.

blowing-kiss.context: A face with puckered lips blowing a kiss, with a small heart floating away. Used for love, affection, goodbyes, thanks and flirty reactions in chat.

holding-phone.context: A hand gripping an upright smartphone with the thumb resting on the screen. Used for mobile apps, phone use, scrolling, screen time and handheld device features.

double-tap-gesture.context: A pointing finger with a tap ripple and the number 2. Used in touchscreen tutorials and settings for double tap to like, zoom or wake the screen.

long-press-gesture.context: A pointing finger pressing down inside a partial progress ring. Used for press and hold, long tap and hold to confirm actions in touchscreen tutorials and settings.

two-finger-scroll.context: A hand with two fingers extended beside a double-headed vertical arrow. Used for two finger scrolling on trackpads and touchscreens in setup guides and settings.

shake-phone-gesture.context: An upright smartphone with curved motion arcs on both sides, showing it being shaken. Used for shake to undo, shake to report and motion gesture settings in mobile apps.

fingerspelling.context: A closed hand shaping a letter beside a capital A. Used for fingerspelling, the manual alphabet and sign language lessons for deaf and hard of hearing learners.

lip-reading.context: An eye above a pair of lips linked by a dotted sight line. Used for lip reading, speechreading, deaf awareness and clear face masks or captions guidance.

flag-semaphore.context: A standing figure holding two diagonally split square flags out at different angles. Used for flag semaphore, maritime and scout signalling and visual communication topics.

traffic-hand-signal.context: A traffic officer in a peaked cap with one arm raised and the other stretched out to the side. Used for traffic control, road safety lessons and police or crossing guard signals.

cycling-hand-signal.context: A cyclist on a bicycle with one arm stretched straight out to signal a turn. Used for road safety, cycling lessons, bike commuting guides and cycle lane rules.

smoke-signal.context: A small campfire with three separate puffs of smoke rising above it. Used for smoke signals, sending a message from afar, camping and wilderness or survival skills.

person-sitting.context: Side view of a person sitting on a stool with the knees bent at a right angle. Used for seating, sitting posture, waiting areas, desk ergonomics and rest.

person-kneeling.context: Side view of a person kneeling on both knees with the upper body upright. Used for kneeling, prayer, gardening, floor work and kneeling posture guides.

person-lying.context: A person lying on their back on the ground with one knee raised. Used for lying down, resting, floor exercises, recovery and sleep or relaxation topics.

person-squatting.context: Side view of a person in a deep squat with the arms held forward for balance. Used for squats, leg workouts, crouching and mobility or fitness exercises.

person-jumping.context: Front view of a person in mid-air with arms and legs spread wide above the ground. Used for jumping, star jumps, excitement, celebration and energetic activity.

hopping.context: A person hopping on one leg with the other leg bent up behind and a line of ground below. Used for hopping, one leg balance, hopscotch, playground games and exercises.

marching.context: Side view of a person marching with one knee raised high and the opposite arm swung forward. Used for marching, parades, protests, military drill and walking exercises.
